Synthetic control for one treated unit

Source: R/synthc.R
synthc.Rd

A weighted average of units never treated that tracks the treated unit before the policy, as its counterfactual after; with the placebo test that runs the same method on every comparison unit.

Usage

synthc(y, unit, time, first, plac = TRUE)

Arguments

y

The outcome: finite numbers, one per row (counts from 0 for fam = "pois" or "nb").

unit

The unit of each row: labels.

time

The period of each row: numbers; a balanced panel.

first

The period the treated unit is first treated, on its rows; NA, 0 or Inf on the rows of the comparison units. Exactly one unit is treated, from a period after the first.

plac

TRUE to run the placebo test.

Value

An object of class synthc, a list: weights (unit, w); path (time, treated, synth, gap); fit, one row: rmspepre, rmspepost, their ratio and the placebo p (NA without the placebos); plac (unit, ratio; NULL without); and unit, the treated unit.

Details

The weights solve min_w sum_{t < T0} (y_1t - sum_j w_j y_jt)^2 over w_j >= 0, sum_j w_j = 1, the periods before adoption T0. The problem is the nearest point of a convex hull to the origin, solved exactly by Wolfe's minimum-norm-point algorithm. The effect in each period is the gap y_1t - sum_j w_j y_jt. For inference each comparison unit in turn is treated as if it had adopted, with the others as its donors; the ratio of the root mean squared gap after adoption to that before ranks the treated unit among the placebos, and p is (1 + the placebos with a ratio at least the treated unit's) / (1 + the placebos) (Abadie, Diamond and Hainmueller 2010). The weights match the outcomes before adoption only, not separate predictors.

References

Abadie, A., Diamond, A. and Hainmueller, J. (2010). Synthetic control methods for comparative case studies. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 105(490), 493-505. doi:10.1198/jasa.2009.ap08746

Wolfe, P. (1976). Finding the nearest point in a polytope. Mathematical Programming, 11, 128-149. doi:10.1007/BF01580381

Examples

d <- expand.grid(year = 2010:2024, town = LETTERS[1:8])
i <- match(d$town, LETTERS)
d$first <- ifelse(d$town == "A", 2019, NA)
d$rate <- 20 + i + (d$year - 2010) * (0.2 + i / 20) +
  sin(seq_len(120)) - 3 * (d$town == "A" & d$year >= 2019)
s <- synthc(d$rate, d$town, d$year, d$first)
s
#> synthc: unit A, root mean squared gap 1.513816 before and 4.813741 after; placebo p 0.125
#>  unit          w
#>     B 0.97743517
#>     C 0.02256483
